cases.original_forecast: The sample consumes about 2 mmol more acid than the blank, corresponding to 1 mmol CaCO3; silica is excluded from neutralising capacity.

cases.title: Recover a known acid spike from a weak-acid sample
cases.original_forecast: The spiked aliquot should require approximately 0.5 mmol more hydroxide, despite a disproportionate change in its starting pH.

cases.title: A titrated aliquot represents the stock only after volume correction
cases.original_forecast: The remaining stock and withdrawn aliquot contain approximately 1.5 and 0.5 mmol acid. Their pre-titration concentrations should agree.

cases.title: Resolve carbonate and bicarbonate with two alkalinity endpoints
cases.original_forecast: The first endpoint requires roughly 0.3 mmol acid and cumulative acid near the second roughly 1.0 mmol. Ideal reconstruction gives n(carbonate)=P and n(bicarbonate)=T−2P.

cases.title: Weigh sulfate in a mixed salt sample rather than all dissolved salts
cases.original_forecast: Approximately 0.5 mmol BaSO4 should be retained, while chloride-rich solution passes into the filtrate; the precipitate is not the total salt mass.

cases.title: Coarse and fine burette steps produce different endpoint uncertainty
cases.original_forecast: The ideal equivalence volume is 10.35 mL. A whole-step endpoint is expected near 11 mL for 1 mL steps and 10.4 mL for 0.1 mL steps, unless the engine explicitly interpolates.

cases.title: Cross-check chloride by gravimetry and standard addition
cases.original_forecast: The calcium-chloride spike introduces 0.4 mmol chloride, so the spiked arm should retain approximately 0.4 mmol more AgCl, not 0.2 mmol.

cases.title: Weak acid plus weak base gives a broad titration endpoint
cases.original_forecast: The weak/weak system changes pH more gradually across equal formal equivalents than the strong/strong control, although proton transfer occurs in both.

cases.title: A hydroxide suspension and its clear filtrate hide different reserves
cases.original_forecast: The suspension can replenish dissolved hydroxide by consuming solid Mg(OH)2. Its filtrate lacks that reserve and should acidify much more under the same acid dose.

cases.title: A carbonate solid moderates repeated acid additions until exhaustion
cases.original_forecast: Acid additions consume carbonate and release inorganic carbon before a strong-acid excess appears. The final 2.5 mmol total acid exceeds the 2 mmol ideal solid capacity.

cases.title: Indicator selection matters for a weak-acid titration
cases.original_forecast: Methyl orange changes in an acidic region and cannot uniquely mark acetic-acid equivalence. Phenolphthalein is responsive in the alkaline region near this titration endpoint.

cases.title: An indicator changes reversibly while its amount stays constant
cases.original_forecast: Bromothymol-blue colour should follow acid–base reversals while the indicator amount is retained; neutralisation changes its environment rather than repeatedly creating dye.

cases.title: The same bicarbonate sample moves in opposite directions under acid and base
cases.original_forecast: Acid favours CO2/carbonic-acid forms, whereas base favours carbonate. The same initial bicarbonate pool therefore displays both sides of amphiprotic behaviour.

cases.title: Equal acid capacities do not imply equal gas production
cases.original_forecast: Both calcium compounds have an ideal capacity of 1 mmol H+ at this loading, but only carbonate supplies 0.5 mmol inorganic carbon and the associated CO2 response.

cases.title: Boiling and carbonate treatment do not remove the same hardness
cases.original_forecast: Heating chloride hardness does not supply carbonate. Soda treatment can remove calcium as a carbonate-bearing solid; boiling alone mainly changes water and concentration.

cases.title: A saturated salt suspension absorbs dilution by dissolving its reservoir
cases.original_forecast: Initially, added water dissolves excess halite and the solution remains near saturation. After the solid reservoir is exhausted, further dilution lowers concentration more directly.

cases.title: Electrode mass changes the inventory, not the equilibrium voltage
cases.original_forecast: With solid metal present in both zinc half-cells, their equilibrium potentials should be similar despite different metal reserves.

cases.title: A finite zinc donor eventually stops depositing fresh copper
cases.original_forecast: Cumulative copper metal deposition cannot substantially exceed the 0.5 mmol zinc electron-donor budget; later copper additions increasingly remain dissolved.

cases.title: Iron oxidation state determines whether iodide is oxidised
cases.original_forecast: Ferric iron can oxidise iodide; ferrous iron is not an equivalent oxidant. Total iron concentration alone does not determine redox capacity.

cases.title: Different current–time pairs deliver the same electrolysis charge
cases.original_forecast: Both commands deliver 5 C. At equal modelled current efficiency their incremental hydrogen and oxygen products should agree.

cases.title: A late stopper cannot recover gas that already escaped
cases.original_forecast: An open-boundary dose can lose carbon before sealing; a closed dose retains its carbon budget. Final states need not agree even with identical nominal additions.

cases.title: A finite alkali trap eventually allows CO2 breakthrough
cases.original_forecast: Initial CO2 is strongly absorbed as carbonate/bicarbonate. As alkalinity is spent, more added carbon remains as dissolved CO2 and headspace gas.

cases.title: Equal carbon amounts need different acid doses before fizzing
cases.original_forecast: The initial acid dose can convert carbonate mainly toward bicarbonate while already liberating more CO2 from the bicarbonate arm. With excess acid, both contain the same original carbon budget.

cases.title: Add a catalyst only after observing the uncatalysed baseline
cases.original_forecast: Peroxide consumption should accelerate after catalyst introduction, relative to the initial uncatalysed interval.

cases.title: Removing a solid catalyst interrupts an ongoing reaction
cases.original_forecast: The catalyst-free filtrate should consume less additional peroxide than the unfiltered control, after correcting for their inventories at filtration.

cases.title: Separate a dissolved nonpolar solute from a soluble salt
cases.original_forecast: The dilute naphthalene can pass the filter but favour the hexane extract, whereas the ionic salt remains mainly aqueous.

cases.title: Cooling before filtration changes what can be recovered
cases.original_forecast: A filter first passes dissolved nitrate solution; cooling the filtrate can produce crystals that a second filtration then retains.

cases.title: Repeated partial washing follows a geometric soluble-impurity budget
cases.original_forecast: Under ideal homogeneous liquid withdrawal, three 80% decants leave about 0.2^3=0.008 of the original dissolved salt with the retained solid.

cases.title: Distillation rejects a nonvolatile salt but may carry a volatile acid
cases.original_forecast: Sodium chloride is largely rejected by distillation, while a represented volatile acetic-acid fraction can enter the condensate and affect its pH.

cases.title: Recover three physical fractions from an immiscible liquid–solid mixture
cases.original_forecast: A lower aqueous fraction, an organic liquid fraction and an insoluble solid residue should be distinguishable, subject to the operators’ actual phase semantics.

cases.title: A magnet distinguishes metallic iron from dissolved iron ions
cases.original_forecast: The model’s ferromagnetic solid operation should collect metallic iron, not remove dissolved Fe(III) merely because the element is iron.

cases.title: Clarification and dissolution are different reasons for a clear liquid
cases.original_forecast: Clarified silica remains as a solid sediment, whereas dissolved salt remains in the liquid. Both may present a clear liquid layer for different reasons.

cases.title: Neutralisation heat is limited by the smaller reagent budget
cases.original_forecast: Both mixtures can neutralise approximately 0.0005 mol of hydroxide, so the neutralisation contribution should be similar rather than doubled. The second mixture retains more excess acid.

cases.title: The same thermometer reading can conceal different stored energies
cases.original_forecast: Both portions can remain near the melting temperature while the more strongly cooled portion contains more ice and a lower retained enthalpy.

cases.title: Equal neutralisation extent, different thermal mass
cases.original_forecast: Both arms can neutralise 0.001 mol, but the less dilute arm should show the larger mixing-corrected temperature rise because it has a smaller thermal mass.

cases.title: Serial dilution: absorbance follows concentration, not total copper
cases.original_forecast: At a common wavelength and optical path, a dilute nonreacting copper chromophore should show falling absorbance as concentration decreases, while total copper remains constant.

cases.title: Filtration can remove scattering without removing dissolved colour
cases.original_forecast: The silica solid should be retained while dissolved copper largely follows the liquid. A scattering-aware optical model may show improved clarity without disappearance of copper absorption.

cases.title: A weaker iodine colour can mean dilution or reduction
cases.original_forecast: Both treatments can weaken iodine-family colour, but dilution preserves oxidised-iodine equivalents while ascorbic acid can reduce iodine to iodide. The spectral changes need not be numerically equal.

cases.title: Distinguish hydroxide contamination from bicarbonate in an alkaline sample
cases.original_forecast: First-endpoint demand P should be near 0.7 mmol and total T near 1.0 mmol. Ideal reconstruction gives n(OH)=2P−T and n(CO3)=T−P.

cases.title: Standardise a permanganate burette against oxalic acid
cases.original_forecast: The stoichiometric requirement is 0.4 mmol permanganate, corresponding to 20 mL of the nominal 0.02 M titrant; a small persistent excess defines the endpoint.

cases.title: Bracket an iodine endpoint with known thiosulfate increments
cases.original_forecast: The ideal endpoint is at a cumulative 0.2 mmol thiosulfate. An endpoint interval, rather than a falsely exact titre, follows from the final dose increments.

cases.title: Back-assay vitamin C using an iodine excess and a reagent blank
cases.original_forecast: After 0.4 mmol thiosulfate, the vitamin-C arm should be near iodine exhaustion while the blank retains about 0.1 mmol iodine equivalents. Their difference represents 0.1 mmol vitamin C.

cases.title: An arbitrary pH-seven endpoint underestimates weak-acid equivalence
cases.original_forecast: The pH-seven stop generally occurs before the weak-acid equivalence region. The higher endpoint requires more base; the difference is endpoint bias, not different acid content.

cases.title: Prepare the same buffer by two stoichiometrically equivalent routes
cases.original_forecast: Both routes target 1 mmol acetic acid, 1 mmol acetate, 2 mmol sodium and 1 mmol chloride. Their pH should be similar after accounting for temperature and small water differences.

cases.title: Recharging a buffer restores pH but accumulates salt
cases.original_forecast: Acid/base recharge approximately restores the buffer ratio while sodium/chloride accumulate. Similar pH values need not imply identical conductivity or ionic strength.

cases.title: Sweeping ammonia changes the composition of a basic buffer
cases.original_forecast: Selective NH3 removal should deplete the base component and lower pH relative to the sealed control; the ammonium/chloride reservoir is not itself a gas.

cases.title: Phosphate protonation state changes at successive base equivalents
cases.original_forecast: One equivalent predominantly gives dihydrogen phosphate; two give hydrogen phosphate; a further half equivalent probes the third, high-pH region. These are different species distributions, not the same neutral salt.

cases.title: Track iron–thiocyanate complex formation with a ligand pulse
cases.original_forecast: Thiocyanate should increase the complex-bound iron fraction and its characteristic optical response without introducing more iron.

cases.title: Exchange a chloride precipitate for a less soluble iodide
cases.original_forecast: AgCl should tend to convert to AgI while chloride is released, if both phases and their exchange equilibrium are represented.

cases.title: Separate magnesium and calcium in two precipitation stages
cases.original_forecast: The first stage preferentially retains magnesium hydroxide; the subsequent carbonate stage targets calcium in the first filtrate.

cases.title: A common-ion wash sacrifices less precipitate than pure water
cases.original_forecast: A modest chloride-containing rinse should reduce AgCl dissolution relative to a pure-water rinse, while both remove soluble impurities.

cases.title: Competing anions share a limited barium budget
cases.original_forecast: Sulfate should strongly compete for barium. Only after sufficient barium is available can substantial carbonate precipitation coexist; neither anion may consume the same barium twice.

cases.title: A buffer resists the hydroxide dose needed to precipitate copper
cases.original_forecast: The acetate-buffered arm spends hydroxide on its acid reserve, delaying extensive copper hydroxide precipitation compared with the unbuffered arm.

cases.title: Acid remobilises phosphate previously captured by calcium
cases.original_forecast: A calcium-phosphate-bearing solid may capture phosphorus from solution; acidification of the isolated solid should favour dissolved phosphate species.

cases.title: Three half-cells form a closed potential-difference triangle
cases.original_forecast: Signed differences should satisfy E13≈E12+E23 when each reading uses the same half-cell states and convention.

cases.title: Diluting both half-cells tests the activity-ratio approximation
cases.original_forecast: An ideal concentration-ratio model predicts little change because both concentrations fall together; real activity and complexation corrections can produce a residual shift.

cases.title: Precipitation can shift a silver electrode without removing its metal
cases.original_forecast: AgCl precipitation lowers free Ag+ activity in one half-cell and can create a concentration-related voltage while both contain silver metal.

cases.title: Reduce silver chloride without first supplying dissolved silver nitrate
cases.original_forecast: Reduction of available silver can draw further AgCl dissolution, yielding silver metal and dissolved zinc/chloride if the coupled phases are represented.

cases.title: Compare one-electron iron with a multi-electron oxidant titre
cases.original_forecast: For the acidic Mn2+ endpoint, 1 mmol Fe(II) supplies the electrons for 0.2 mmol permanganate, nominally 10 mL titrant.

cases.title: Pass reducing equivalents through a recovered copper intermediate
cases.original_forecast: Copper recovered from zinc displacement can reduce silver ions in a second stage. The interpretation depends on confirming that residual zinc is not the direct silver donor.

cases.title: Copper depletion changes what additional electrolysis charge can produce
cases.original_forecast: The 0.05 mmol copper inventory can accept only about 9.65 C for complete Cu(II)-to-Cu reduction. Further charge cannot create more copper than supplied.

cases.title: Release and recapture ammonia inside one closed system
cases.original_forecast: Base favours NH3; subsequent acid returns nitrogen toward ammonium and lowers its gas-phase share without removing total nitrogen.

cases.title: A closed warming–cooling cycle redistributes carbon rather than losing it
cases.original_forecast: Warming changes gas pressure and CO2 partitioning. Cooling toward the original temperature should approximately restore the partition without needing a new carbon dose.

cases.title: More liquid can retain more CO2 at the same headspace size
cases.original_forecast: The larger water volume should hold a larger fraction of the finite carbon dose, reducing its gas-phase pressure contribution relative to the small-water arm.

cases.title: Respiration can alter pressure despite equal formal O2 and CO2 coefficients
cases.original_forecast: The requested overall route consumes 6 O2 and forms 6 CO2 per glucose. Gas pressure need not be unchanged because CO2 and O2 partition differently and water is also formed.

cases.title: Recover captured carbon from an isolated carbonate solid
cases.original_forecast: Captured carbonate carbon should remain with the isolated solid and reappear as CO2/dissolved carbon on acidification; uncaptured carbon stays in the earlier liquid/gas accounts.

cases.title: Different catalyst masses can have the same nominal surface area
cases.original_forecast: For the same material and spherical-particle approximation, mass/diameter is matched, so the two nominal surface-controlled responses should be similar.

cases.title: Grinding an existing catalyst changes its future activity, not past yield
cases.original_forecast: Reducing particle size should increase subsequent surface-mediated consumption. The grind command itself must not retrospectively generate the previous interval’s extra products.

cases.title: Splitting a homogeneous reacting solution preserves fractional kinetics
cases.original_forecast: If enzyme and substrate transfer proportionally, both portions retain the same concentrations and should show similar fractional peroxide depletion, while absolute consumption scales with volume.

cases.title: First-order half-life is tested by changing initial substrate, not the clock
cases.original_forecast: At matched catalyst activity and temperature, a first-order surface teaching model predicts similar fractions remaining, despite different absolute initial substrate.

cases.title: Cooling an active catalytic mixture slows the next interval
cases.original_forecast: Cooling should lower the rate coefficient of the ongoing MnO2/peroxide model, separate from the decline caused by substrate depletion.

cases.title: Neutralisation quenches an acid-driven sulfur clock
cases.original_forecast: Base removes available acidity and should strongly suppress further sulfur formation; renewed acid can restart conversion of remaining thiosulfate.

cases.title: Removing the visible sulfur does not remove all unreacted precursor
cases.original_forecast: If acid and thiosulfate remain in the filtrate, fresh sulfur can form there after the original solid is retained in the first vessel.

cases.title: A recovered reaction product becomes a catalyst for a second reaction
cases.original_forecast: If the first route produces MnO2, its isolated solid should accelerate peroxide decomposition relative to the catalyst-free control.

cases.title: Strip iodine from an organic extract by reducing it
cases.original_forecast: Reduction should convert extractable iodine into more water-favouring iodide, enabling reactive back-extraction into the newly added aqueous phase.

cases.title: Centrifugal acceleration depends quadratically on rotation speed
cases.original_forecast: At equal radius, ideal centrifugal acceleration scales as rpm squared; the higher-speed arm should show greater settling if the model resolves the regime.

cases.title: Particle diameter changes sedimentation at fixed centrifuge settings
cases.original_forecast: Larger particles should settle more readily in a dilute Stokes-like regime; equal solid mass does not imply equal separation speed.

cases.title: Crystallise nitrate selectively from a mixed-salt solution
cases.original_forecast: Cooling should favour potassium-nitrate crystallisation while the smaller sodium-chloride charge may remain largely in solution.

cases.title: Extraction recovery should depend on phase ratio rather than batch scale
cases.original_forecast: At matched composition and phase-volume ratio, an ideal dilute partition model predicts similar fractional naphthalene recovery despite a twofold batch scale.

cases.title: Hess-law route comparison: lime hydration before neutralisation
cases.original_forecast: If both routes reach the same retained composition without different losses, their complete-route enthalpy balances should agree. Intermediate heat changes differ because hydration and neutralisation are separated in the second route.

cases.title: Infer ice-melting energy from a measured warm-water balance
cases.original_forecast: Warm water first supplies sensible and latent energy to the cold portion. The final temperature should fall below a liquid-only weighted-temperature prediction when initial ice is present.

cases.title: Freeze concentration and recovery of a lower-salt melt
cases.original_forecast: An ice-excluding salt model predicts enriched brine in the filtrate and a lower-salt melt from the retained ice. Compare concentrations after accounting for different water masses.

cases.title: Pressure shifts the boiling plateau under the same heat input
cases.original_forecast: A pressure-aware phase model predicts a higher water boiling temperature at 2 bar and a different sensible-versus-latent allocation of the same heat.

cases.title: Mass-specific versus molar heat capacities of two metals
cases.original_forecast: Equal-mass samples have different temperature rises. For these metals near room temperature, the equal-mole comparison is expected to be closer because molar heat capacities are more similar than mass-specific values.

cases.title: Salt-induced melting can cool an ice-water mixture
cases.original_forecast: When supported by the coupled brine/ice model, salt lowers the freezing equilibrium temperature and promotes melting that consumes latent energy. Cooling and melting can therefore occur together.

cases.title: Assay residual acid after a requested esterification
cases.original_forecast: If only the requested first arm esterifies, its remaining acid demand should be lower than the unactivated feed control. The titration-derived difference should be checked against the pre-workup ester inventory.

cases.title: Quantify acidity produced by requested ethanol oxidation
cases.original_forecast: The activated arm should generate titratable acetic acid in proportion to ethanol converted. The unactivated arm tests whether an explicit named reaction is required.

cases.title: Capture carbon from the requested glucose-respiration model
cases.original_forecast: The requested respiration can release up to 0.0006 mol of carbon dioxide from this glucose dose. Lime addition may transfer some of that carbon into carbonate solid while the rest remains in dissolved or gaseous pools.

cases.title: Back-titration assay of an ester with excess hydroxide
cases.original_forecast: For complete hydrolysis, the activated sample should consume about 0.0005 mol less strong acid than the base blank at an endpoint that mostly leaves acetate deprotonated.

cases.title: Conductivity can change with temperature at fixed salt inventory
cases.original_forecast: A temperature-dependent transport model can change conductivity during warming even though sodium and chloride totals are unchanged. Cooling tests reversibility rather than chemical consumption.

cases.title: Chromatographic tracking of an ester-hydrolysis intermediate
cases.original_forecast: If the chromatograph recognises the relevant molecular pools, ester features should decrease and ethanol features increase as additional hydroxide permits further hydrolysis.

cases.title: Compare mixed and single-component buffers across two pH regions
cases.original_forecast: The mixed acetate/phosphate sample should retain an additional buffering region after the acetate-only sample approaches exhaustion.

cases.title: Use continuous variation to test complex stoichiometry
cases.original_forecast: Under a dominant 1:1 FeSCN model, the complex-specific response should peak near the equal-mole mixture, not at the largest iron input.

cases.title: A competing phosphate pool can remove iron from a coloured complex
cases.original_forecast: Phosphate may decrease the Fe–SCN fraction through competing aqueous or solid species; the extra-acid arm helps reveal whether acidity alone explains the response.

cases.title: Acid can selectively remove carbonate from a silver precipitate mixture
cases.original_forecast: Acid destabilises a carbonate-bearing silver solid while AgCl is comparatively retained; liberated silver may redistribute according to chloride availability.

cases.title: Background electrolyte tests concentration versus activity in a cell
cases.original_forecast: A salt-induced activity-coefficient change can shift the predicted cell voltage even with unchanged analytical copper and zinc amounts.

cases.title: Two catalysts do not justify multiplying their speed-up factors
cases.original_forecast: The combined-catalyst response must follow an explicit pathway-combination rule; multiplying two observed acceleration factors is not a justified chemical prediction.

cases.title: An iodine sink changes induction time without requiring a faster source reaction
cases.original_forecast: A larger thiosulfate sink can delay iodine accumulation even if the underlying iodine-production kinetics are similar.

cases.title: Hydrolyse an ester, then oxidise the liberated alcohol
cases.original_forecast: Successful sequential transformations first yield acetate and ethanol, then convert the ethanol fraction into another acetate/acetic-acid family pool. Carbon accounting should retain four carbons per initial ester molecule.

cases.title: Extract an esterification mixture and assay both product pools
cases.original_forecast: If partition data and molecular-pool coupling are present, ester, acid and ethanol should have distinguishable extraction fractions. Each component must be reconciled across both vessels.

cases.title: Standard addition with volume-corrected optical responses
cases.original_forecast: Successive known copper additions should increase a supported copper optical signal, but changing volume requires correction before interpreting the response per added mole.

cases.title: Starch digestion: sample before adding the iodine indicator
cases.original_forecast: Enzymatic chain cleavage should reduce the starch-associated colour relative to the intact-starch control; maltose is not an intact amylose helix. Inspect substrate/product inventory as well as colour.

cases.title: Lactase acts on the milk substrate pool, not on free glucose
cases.original_forecast: The supported milk substrate can acquire a lactose-hydrolysis state; glucose alone should not be counted as lactose. The milk remains a conserved aggregate, not newly resolved glucose and galactose species.

cases.title: Protein versus sugar enzymes on the same gelatin sample
cases.original_forecast: Protease should generate a protein-hydrolysis state whereas lactase and the blank should not. This alone does not establish that a visible gelatin gel has liquefied.

cases.title: Sugar conversion can occur without gas production
cases.original_forecast: Alcoholic conversion should produce ethanol and CO2; homolactic conversion should produce lactic acid without stoichiometric CO2. A low gas signal therefore does not establish that sugar was unchanged.

cases.title: Yeast does not make starch an automatically fermentable sugar
cases.original_forecast: The sucrose vessel should support the installed alcoholic route; intact starch should not simply be relabelled as sugar and fermented by the same culture.

cases.title: Polymer identity cannot be reduced to a single float/sink test
cases.original_forecast: Use the installed material densities and observed phase inventory to classify candidates, while recognising that PE/PP and denser polymers cannot all be uniquely identified by one threshold.

cases.title: A PVA network requires both polymer and borate
cases.original_forecast: The combined vessel should report the bounded borate/PVA network state, while either-component controls should not. Do not count network formation as disappearance of all PVA and borate molecules.

cases.title: Thermoplastic and thermoset under the same thermal cycle
cases.original_forecast: The PE-based article can cross its declared softening threshold and return to a rigid state on cooling. The cured network should not be labelled melt-processable merely because it is warm.

cases.title: A superabsorbent stores water without consuming it
cases.original_forecast: Retained water should be bounded by the installed polymer capacity; additional water beyond that capacity remains available rather than creating extra polymer or disappearing.

cases.title: The same repeat-unit formula does not mean the same enzyme substrate
cases.original_forecast: Starch cleavage can occur without analogous cellulose cleavage. The two materials should not be treated as interchangeable simply because a formula parser sees the same repeat-unit atom counts.

cases.title: Stirring and surfactant are separate emulsion requirements
cases.original_forecast: The supported oil-plus-surfactant system should acquire a temporary dispersed state after stirring. The no-surfactant and unstirred preparations distinguish composition from mechanical action.

cases.title: An aging emulsion can be dispersed again
cases.original_forecast: A declining dispersion state followed by renewed dispersion without fresh chemical ingredients is a physical history, not evidence that the oil was destroyed and re-synthesized.

cases.title: An oil layer is not a dissolved organic molecule
cases.original_forecast: Ethanol belongs to the mixed liquid solvent inventory, whereas the oil recipe can retain an immiscible-layer state. Organic composition alone does not determine miscibility.

cases.title: Curdling is different from making milk less opaque by dilution
cases.original_forecast: Review the explicit curdling/aggregate state separately from opacity. Dilution should not be labelled protein coagulation merely because the sample looks less white.

cases.title: Foam volume is not the number of moles of gas
cases.original_forecast: Foam can persist in the surfactant vessel even though the bicarbonate-limited gas yield is comparable. Its later collapse is not conversion of CO2 back into bicarbonate.

cases.title: Surface motion need not be a reaction of the floating solid
cases.original_forecast: Compare the bounded surface-spread response with a water-addition control; no pepper-reaction product should be invented to explain physical redistribution.

cases.title: Two natural pigments can share a colour without sharing a spectrum
cases.original_forecast: Compare band patterns with their own solvent blanks rather than equating colour intensity or absorbance to equal molecular amounts. Any unparameterised pigment must remain explicitly unparameterised.

cases.title: A plant indicator can trace an acid-base round trip
cases.original_forecast: Correlate any pigment response with measured pH at all three points. A return in colour is evidence for an acid-base-associated state only where the pigment model actually exposes that response.

cases.title: Bleaching a pigment is different from diluting it
cases.original_forecast: The supported bleaching route can create an oxidised-pigment surrogate, whereas dilution should retain the starting pigment identity. The reagent blank separates oxidant background from dye signal.

cases.title: Chemical light does not require an external light source
cases.original_forecast: Only the complete prepared formulation plus activator should produce its declared emission state. There is no incoming-light command, separating chemical emission from ordinary illuminated appearance.

cases.title: Opaque pigment mixing is not averaging two RGB colours
cases.original_forecast: The mixture should use the installed pigment absorption/scattering model rather than a naïve arithmetic colour average. All pigment material remains present after mixing.

cases.title: A filter does not remove a dissolved dye by itself
cases.original_forecast: The charcoal treatment can transfer part of the supported dye to a retained adsorbed pool; the filter-only control should not remove a truly dissolved dye solely because it is coloured.

cases.title: Clear water can still contain dissolved salt
cases.original_forecast: The supported dye may be adsorbed while sodium and chloride remain in the aqueous pool. Interpret optical and conductivity evidence together; decolourisation is not desalination.

cases.title: Hydrated and anhydrous magnesium sulfate: compare formula units, not grams
cases.original_forecast: Both inputs carry the same number of MgSO4 formula units, but epsomite includes seven waters per unit. Final concentration and thermal behavior need not be identical with the same separately added solvent.

cases.title: Heating does not increase every mineral solubility
cases.original_forecast: Compare the dissolved/solid inventories before and after heating at the actual temperatures. The registered gypsum relation is retrograde over its reference range, unlike the common positive KNO3 trend.

cases.title: Carbonate and sulfate minerals do not share the same acid-test signal
cases.original_forecast: The carbonate route supplies inorganic carbon and potentially retained CO2; gypsum supplies calcium/sulfate without a stoichiometric carbon-gas source. Confirm gas identity from inventory rather than pressure alone.

cases.title: Magnetic recovery does not measure all the iron in a mixture
cases.original_forecast: Reconcile what the magnetic operation actually moves with the metallic and oxide identities. The recovered fraction must not be reported as total elemental iron without accounting for iron remaining in hematite.

cases.title: A flame fingerprint follows the cation, not the whole salt name
cases.original_forecast: Compare the declared emission signatures of NaCl, NaBr and KCl and check that a flame-test event does not consume each salt as fuel. An unparameterised salt must be reported as such rather than assigned a guessed line.

cases.title: A mixture needs a mixture interpretation of its flame signal
cases.original_forecast: Use both reference signatures and the known mixed inventory. Whether the engine renders one colour or several, the mixture must not be classified as a pure compound from a single dominant visual cue.

cases.title: Compare chloride, bromide and iodide precipitate fingerprints
cases.original_forecast: Look for halide-specific silver solids and compare them with the reagent blank. Where colour is reported, use it as one clue alongside the explicit solid identity, not a complete blind assay.

cases.title: Vitamin C can hide starch from an iodine test
cases.original_forecast: Initial iodine can be consumed by the reductant before it creates a strong starch signal. A later iodine excess can reveal retained starch, separating indicator destruction from substrate absence.

cases.title: Triangulate a solvent identity from independent physical properties
cases.original_forecast: Build a multi-property fingerprint from reported values and provenance. Similar density does not imply identical molecular identity, and a property lookup should not be called an experimentally observed boiling curve.

cases.title: Conductivity can detect an electrolyte without identifying its anion
cases.original_forecast: Both halide solutions are electrolyte candidates while sucrose is a nonelectrolyte reference. A similar or colourless response is not proof that chloride and bromide are the same species.

cases.title: A neighbouring metal can protect iron or leave it anodic
cases.original_forecast: Review anodic/cathodic roles and actual metal consumption. Zinc can protect iron while it remains available; copper does not play the same sacrificial role. Do not infer a calibrated acceleration factor for the iron/copper pair.

cases.title: Carbon allotropes can have very different electronic behaviour
cases.original_forecast: Compare the installed solid-state electrical descriptors for graphite and diamond with a metal and a polymer reference. Shared carbon composition is not evidence of the same bonding topology or electronic structure.

cases.title: Chain length can change room-temperature phase behaviour
cases.original_forecast: Use the pure-stock transition descriptors and actual inventories to distinguish a liquid lower homologue from a higher homologue that may cross a nearby solid/liquid transition.

cases.title: Two alcohols can have similar boiling behaviour but very different freezing behaviour
cases.original_forecast: Compare melting and boiling descriptors rather than treating the hydroxyl functional group as a complete prediction of physical behavior. The warming step tests any installed near-ambient phase change.

cases.title: A baking-powder formulation is not just sodium bicarbonate
cases.original_forecast: Compare the formulation with its approximately matched bicarbonate contribution. The runtime must explicitly account for any release of formulation components or additional reaction, rather than attributing everything to bicarbonate alone.

cases.title: An antioxidant response is not a food-safety verdict
cases.original_forecast: The bounded cut-surface model can show less visible browning with ascorbate under comparable oxygen exposure. That response is not proof of sterility, edibility or unchanged flavour.

cases.title: A formulation can contain both a gas source and a starch-test target
cases.original_forecast: The formulation's declared starch fraction can produce an iodine-associated response while bicarbonate alone should not. This diagnoses an ingredient, not the gas-forming capacity of the whole powder.

cases.title: A watercolour and an acrylic paint can carry blue colour differently
cases.original_forecast: Compare dissolved-species coverage with unresolved pigment/binder states. A blue appearance is not evidence that both paints have the same molecular colourant or obey the same optical dilution law.

cases.title: Pepsin activity in acidic and neutral protein suspensions
cases.original_forecast: The acid enzyme-containing vessel should show more modelled protein hydrolysis than the neutral enzyme vessel. The acid-only control separates the enzyme state from acidity alone.

cases.title: Heating the enzyme source rather than the protein substrate
cases.original_forecast: If the heated source crosses its declared denaturation threshold, its later proteolytic activity should remain lower after cooling. The comparison is about enzyme history, not heating gelatin itself.

cases.title: Lipase recognises oil, not cellulose
cases.original_forecast: Only the oil-plus-lipase vessel should acquire the supported triglyceride-hydrolysis state. Neither dissolved glycerol nor liberated fatty acids may be claimed unless the actual runtime explicitly resolves them.

cases.title: Add fresh protein after a protease incubation
cases.original_forecast: Newly supplied protein should contribute a fresh hydrolysable pool in the enzyme vessel. Track the mass-weighted converted fraction rather than treating an apparent fraction decrease after feeding as reversal.

cases.title: Selective digestion in a mixed milk-and-gelatin matrix
cases.original_forecast: Lactase should act on the declared milk-sugar pool; protease should act on the declared gelatin-protein pool. The combined treatment should preserve separate material identities rather than report one generic digestion percentage.

cases.title: Pause and resume the pepsin pH gate
cases.original_forecast: Compare incremental, not cumulative, hydrolysis across acidic, near-neutral and reacidified intervals. Activity may recover in the final interval if the pH gate is restored.

cases.title: Sourdough allocates carbon to acid, alcohol and gas
cases.original_forecast: Look for acid, ethanol and CO2 together and account for the starter recipe's own sugar. Chromatography alone cannot close the balance because ionised acid and unsupported components may be outside that method.

cases.title: Compare fresh and dry yeast on a dry-solids basis
cases.original_forecast: The first two preparations approximately match yeast solids and recipe water, unlike the equal-weighed-mass comparison. Early differences can also reflect the dry-yeast hydration state.

cases.title: The milk matrix changes what acidification can tell you
cases.original_forecast: Both cultured samples can generate lactic acid, but their pH changes need not scale directly with converted sugar because the milk has additional material and mineral pools. Use recorded conversion to interpret pH.

cases.title: Cold storage followed by warming is a history, not a new culture
cases.original_forecast: Compare conversion increments before and after warming against the warm-start control. The temperature envelope should change ongoing activity, not create a new population.

cases.title: Change the separating liquid, not the plastic sample
cases.original_forecast: Compare measured liquid density with each polymer density. A denser brine may cross the PS threshold while remaining below PET, allowing a different classification than pure water.

cases.title: Network loading differs from simply adding more polymer
cases.original_forecast: The polymer-normalised cross-linker loading changes after each addition. Distinguish networked fraction from total networked mass and inspect that all inputs remain conserved.

cases.title: Polar polymer chains need not dissolve in water
cases.original_forecast: Compare installed phase assignments rather than claiming that all polar materials dissolve. The small-molecule reference and polymer samples illustrate competition among hydration, packing and chain interactions.

cases.title: Fatty soap and generic detergent are not interchangeable in hard water
cases.original_forecast: Only the declared fatty-soap equivalent supports the aggregate calcium-soap binding claim. A generic detergent role must not automatically be interpreted as sodium stearate.

cases.title: Curcumin colour and a neutral solvent blank
cases.original_forecast: The mixed-solvent blank should not acquire a curcumin band. Interpret a pigment response together with measured pH and coverage, rather than assuming every pH shift has a fully parameterised spectrum.

cases.title: Brightness and persistence can trade off
cases.original_forecast: Compare reported relative intensity and decay state over time. A brighter initial display must not be described as a larger total chemical yield without an independently supported photon/energy balance.

cases.title: A sunscreen model has spectral bands, not one universal shield factor
cases.original_forecast: Review band-specific incident and transmitted-state information rather than assigning the UVB protection factor to every wavelength. The water-only vessel is a formulation-omission control.

cases.title: An adsorbent can saturate before the water becomes colourless
cases.original_forecast: Track free and adsorbed dye after the loading and sorbent-rescue steps. Finite capacity should prevent unlimited removal by a fixed mass of charcoal.

cases.title: A treatment train removes different kinds of contamination differently
cases.original_forecast: Review which solids remain after the first filter, where the dye resides after charcoal contact, and which dissolved ions persist in the final filtrate. No single visual observation certifies complete treatment.

cases.title: A sulfate background and an ionic-strength control affect gypsum differently
cases.original_forecast: Sulfate participates in the gypsum dissolution equilibrium; chloride does not play the same common-ion role. The controls are not exactly ionic-strength matched, so use speciation rather than a pure concentration argument.

cases.title: Acid cleaning: metal consumption and oxide dissolution are not the same reaction
cases.original_forecast: Metal oxidation by acid can form hydrogen, whereas acid dissolution of the oxide does not itself require hydrogen evolution. The iron oxidation states and acid demands also differ.

cases.title: Iodide changes iodine availability without being extra iodine molecules
cases.original_forecast: Interpret polyiodide-associated dissolved iodine in the iodide vessel separately from total added iodine atoms. Chloride does not provide the same iodine/iodide association mechanism.

cases.title: A barrier coating is not another dissolved corrosion inhibitor
cases.original_forecast: Compare the material-role barrier with bare iron of approximately matched iron mass. A paint-origin accessibility rule should not be reported as an acid-base reaction or as conversion of paint into a corrosion product.

cases.title: Passivated alloy and bare iron are not equivalent aqueous inputs
cases.original_forecast: The declared passive-film accessibility rule can distinguish the alloy material from bare iron. The result must not be generalized to immunity of all stainless steels in every chloride environment.

cases.title: Two cold additions need not have the same acid-base effect
cases.original_forecast: Any CO2 retained in water can participate in carbonate acid-base chemistry; nitrogen does not provide the same acid source. Equal cryogen masses do not imply equal cooling or equal dissolved-gas amounts.

cases.title: Sublimation and boiling are different phase-change paths
cases.original_forecast: Distinguish solid-to-gas CO2 and liquid-to-gas nitrogen pathways where their explicit phase models are supported. Open-system inventory loss must be assigned to exported gas, not destruction of atoms.

cases.title: Molecular products and aggregate conversion are different outputs
cases.original_forecast: Review both inventories: any molecular maltose production belongs to the installed starch route, while lactase conversion belongs to a milk-material annotation. Neither should create unexplained mass.

cases.title: A two-stage sugar-to-acid bioprocess
cases.original_forecast: Review sugar-to-ethanol conversion before introducing the second culture. Afterwards, any acetic-acid increase must be reconciled with loss of ethanol and finite available oxygen.

cases.title: An oxygen pulse can restart a limited acetification step
cases.original_forecast: Reconcile the initial headspace and both oxygen additions with any further acetic-acid formation. A second pulse can increase conversion only when a supported ethanol pool remains.

cases.title: A polymer blend does not have one guaranteed pure melting point
cases.original_forecast: Use the pure references to interpret the mixture output. A single returned property must not be presented as an experimentally established blend transition or proof of blend miscibility.

cases.title: A thermoplastic article and its repeat-unit stock are not identical objects
cases.original_forecast: Both inputs contain the PE chemical identity, but only the named article necessarily carries its material-role softening annotation. Do not interpret an absent annotation as proof that real bare PE cannot melt.

cases.title: Separate light scattering from a dissolved pigment signal
cases.original_forecast: Compare pigment-associated bands with the cloudy blank; do not interpret total attenuation as dye concentration. A post-centrifugation claim requires an actually reported material redistribution.

cases.title: Recover dye from a loaded adsorbent by changing the surrounding solution
cases.original_forecast: Fresh wash water can allow some dye to leave a reversible adsorbed pool. Account for dye in both filtrates and the remaining charcoal rather than assuming every wash removes it completely.

cases.title: Two fresh adsorption stages versus one larger stage
cases.original_forecast: Compare the single-stage filtrate with the two-stage filtrate at equal total sorbent mass. Any advantage comes from renewed equilibrium contact with fresh surface, not extra sorbent hidden in the setup.

cases.title: A conservative salt pulse followed by a clean-water chase
cases.original_forecast: The tracer pulse should pass downstream and enter the collected effluent, followed by clean water. Reconcile initial cell inventory plus cumulative injected tracer with final cells plus effluent.

cases.title: Numerical dispersion is not a new chemical reaction
cases.original_forecast: The schemes can distribute the same injected tracer over different cells and collection histories while conserving its amount. Do not label numerical front spreading as diffusion chemistry.

cases.title: An acid front advances through a carbonate-containing bed
cases.original_forecast: Acid neutralisation and carbonate dissolution can occur locally before an acidic effluent develops. Reconcile the repeated boundary injection with remaining mineral and dissolved/gas carbon inventories.

cases.title: Mobile ions can create a stationary precipitate
cases.original_forecast: Look for AgCl formation and retention in the cell that owns it. The initially dissolved silver is also mobile, so the precipitation location must come from the coupled update rather than being assumed in advance.

cases.title: Temperature can be transported without a reacting solute
cases.original_forecast: Review the moving thermal perturbation and integrated outlet temperature with the injected energy ledger. Temperature change alone does not establish an exothermic or endothermic reaction.

cases.title: Sorption can delay a dye relative to a salt tracer
cases.original_forecast: If reactive transport refreshes the installed adsorption equilibrium, charcoal-bound dye can lag a conservative ion tracer. The actual free and bound dye inventory must demonstrate this coupling.

cases.title: Mineral dissolution supplies an outlet even with a solute-free inlet
cases.original_forecast: Calcium/sulfate exported downstream must be matched by a decrease in the original gypsum inventory. Fresh inlet water can sustain dissolution while mineral remains.

cases.title: A metal bed can transform an incoming dissolved-metal stream
cases.original_forecast: A supported displacement/transport coupling can retain deposited copper while transferring oxidised iron downstream. The conclusion must come from element and oxidation-state accounting, not colour alone.

cases.title: Equal copper amounts need not give the same mineral acid demand
cases.original_forecast: The doses contain equal total copper but different hydroxide counts and counteranions. If both minerals dissolve, residual acidity and released anions can differ even when copper-associated signals are similar.

cases.title: A hydrated patina mineral carries more than its copper and sulfate
cases.original_forecast: Compare the declared mineral formulas and any dissolution ledger. The hydration difference changes initial mass and potentially solvent water, not the number of copper atoms per chosen formula-unit dose.

cases.title: Primary haloalkane: substitution and elimination give different product classes
cases.original_forecast: The installed table selects substitution in the cooler branch and elimination in the hotter branch: ethanol versus ethene, both with bromide-containing products. Establish product identity from inventory, not simply a pressure difference between hot and cool vessels.

cases.title: Tertiary solvolysis produces an acidic coproduct
cases.original_forecast: The supported solvolysis branch can form tert-butanol and HBr-derived aqueous species. The solvent blank separates coproduct acidity from a nominal starting-water property.

cases.title: Tertiary substrate plus strong base is not automatically an SN2 example
cases.original_forecast: The table can select primary substitution but tertiary elimination under strong-base conditions. Use the product inventories to identify structural selectivity rather than treating all haloalkanes as interchangeable.

cases.title: Solvolysis and thermal elimination share a leaving group, not a product
cases.original_forecast: The cool branch can give tert-butanol; the hot branch can give isobutylene. Both can release an acidic bromide coproduct, so pH alone cannot identify the organic mechanism.

cases.title: Ionic solids do not all have the same solubility in a dry organic solvent
cases.original_forecast: Review each installed organic-solvent solubility verdict and residual solid. Any dissolved salt is treated by this limited route as an undissociated solute, not as a fully speciated aqueous electrolyte.

cases.title: A neutral organic blend needs more than one chromatographic peak label
cases.original_forecast: Compare available component predictions with the mixture and explicitly retain the method's unsupported-component list. Equal introduced moles do not guarantee equal measured peak areas or perfect resolution.

cases.title: Ionisation can change the method coverage of an organic acid
cases.original_forecast: Compare neutral acid and ionised acetate inventories with the chromatogram's coverage categories. Loss of a neutral peak must not be described as destruction of all acetic-acid-derived carbon.

cases.title: Sacrificial protection has a finite inventory
cases.original_forecast: Track whether zinc actually depletes and whether oxygen remains before interpreting a transition to accessible iron corrosion. A time interval alone is not evidence that the protection failed.

cases.title: Doping can change electrical properties without a visible bulk-density change
cases.original_forecast: The selected doped-silicon grade can have a different electrical descriptor from intrinsic silicon while retaining similar bulk density. A density-only assay cannot establish electronic purity.

cases.title: A wax surrogate is not a chemically pure phase-change standard
cases.original_forecast: Contrast the wax surrogate's declared property model with a named molecular hydrocarbon. A single transition value returned for paraffin is not evidence that commercial paraffin wax is one pure compound.

cases.title: Equal molar gas amounts need not have equal heat capacity
cases.original_forecast: Interpret temperature changes using the whole reported gas inventory and its thermal model. Equal added moles do not guarantee equal total heat capacity, especially if pre-existing headspace gas is present.

cases.title: Known boundary: salt sensitivity is absent from the simple swelling model
cases.original_forecast: The reviewed implementation uses water availability and a fixed polymer capacity, not ionic environment. An unchanged predicted retention state should be recorded as that limitation, not a finding that real polyelectrolyte gels are salt-insensitive.

cases.title: Known boundary: emulsifying oil need not speed the aggregate lipase model
cases.original_forecast: Review emulsion and hydrolysis outputs independently. The aggregate substrate-dose model does not establish a droplet-area rate law; equal hydrolysis despite different dispersion must not be reported as a general real-lipase result.

cases.title: An irradiation command is not proof of a supported photochemical pathway
cases.original_forecast: Photochemical conversion is established only if runtime exposes a supported light-dependent route and a consistent reagent/product ledger beyond the dark control. Merely accepting irradiate or displaying a wavelength is not such evidence.

cases.title: A missing chromatographic peak does not prove a missing ingredient
cases.original_forecast: Compare the peak list with the independent salt and unresolved-protein inventories. A plot that includes ethanol cannot certify absence of the other ingredients, whether or not every omission is explicitly labelled by the instrument.

cases.title: Conductometric strong-acid titration: a minimum, not only an endpoint
cases.original_physical_forecast: Conductivity falls as highly mobile hydrogen ions are replaced by sodium ions, reaches a minimum near equivalence, and rises with excess hydroxide.

cases.title: Weak-acid conductometric titration distinguishes neutralisation from dilution
cases.original_physical_forecast: Formation of sodium acetate increases the mobile-ion inventory; after equivalence, excess hydroxide gives a steeper conductivity rise.

cases.title: Resolve the first two phosphoric-acid equivalence regions
cases.original_physical_forecast: The pH curve contains separate first- and second-proton neutralisation regions; half-equivalent mixtures reveal two different buffers.

cases.title: Sulfuric acid needs two base equivalents per formula unit
cases.original_physical_forecast: One equivalent leaves bisulfate acidity; two equivalents give a sulfate-dominated solution without a large strong-acid reserve.

cases.title: Bicarbonate is amphiprotic, unlike strongly basic carbonate
cases.original_physical_forecast: At equal analytical carbon loading, bicarbonate is moderately basic and carbonate is appreciably more alkaline.

cases.title: Build an ammonium–ammonia buffer by half-neutralisation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Half-neutralisation creates an NH4+/NH3 buffer. A small acid challenge changes its ratio rather than causing an unbuffered pH collapse.

cases.title: An acetate buffer absorbs hydroxide by spending its acid component
cases.original_physical_forecast: Hydroxide consumes acetic acid and raises the acetate/acid ratio, causing only a moderate pH increase.

cases.title: Equal buffer pH does not mean equal buffer capacity
cases.original_physical_forecast: The buffers start at similar pH, but the ten-times larger acid/base pool resists the same acid challenge more effectively.

cases.title: Similar initial pH can conceal very different acid reserves
cases.original_physical_forecast: These doses give roughly similar initial pH in an ideal calculation. The base challenge exhausts the strong-acid dose while leaving acetic acid in a buffer.

cases.title: A conjugate-base salt hydrolyses even with no added alkali
cases.original_physical_forecast: Sodium acetate solution is more alkaline than a sodium chloride control because acetate accepts protons from water.

cases.title: A phosphate buffer protects near-neutral pH
cases.original_physical_forecast: A phosphate mixture between its first and second neutralisation equivalents resists an acid pulse that strongly acidifies water.

cases.title: Mixing pH values is not taking their arithmetic mean
cases.original_physical_forecast: Equal volumes of approximately pH 2 and pH 4 strong acid mix to about pH 2.3 in the ideal approximation, not pH 3.

cases.title: Hydroxide equivalents depend on formula stoichiometry
cases.original_physical_forecast: Equal formula-unit amounts of NaOH and Ca(OH)2 consume different proton amounts: one and two equivalents respectively.

cases.title: Compare antacid capacity per gram without confusing fizz with neutralisation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Both solids consume two protons per formula unit, but the smaller molar mass of Mg(OH)2 gives greater acid capacity per gram. Only carbonate produces CO2.

cases.title: Zinc hydroxide precipitates, then dissolves in excess base
cases.original_physical_forecast: A moderate hydroxide dose gives Zn(OH)2; sufficiently strong excess hydroxide can redissolve it into soluble hydroxo-zinc species.

cases.title: Dissolve magnesium hydroxide and reprecipitate it
cases.original_physical_forecast: Acid dissolves the initial hydroxide; restoring alkalinity produces a magnesium hydroxide solid again without inventing a magnesium-chloride bottle key.

cases.title: Ferric hydroxide redissolves when its pH support is removed
cases.original_physical_forecast: Brown ferric hydroxide formed by base addition is substantially removed by a deliberate excess of acid.

cases.title: An acid reserve can prevent calcium carbonate precipitation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Without prior acid, carbonate precipitates calcium. With excess proton capacity, carbonate is protonated and the calcium mostly remains dissolved.

cases.title: Limewater clouds and then clears under excess carbon dioxide
cases.original_physical_forecast: Initial CO2 converts hydroxide into calcium carbonate; excess retained CO2 lowers pH and favours dissolved calcium/bicarbonate.

cases.title: Purify impure limestone by dissolution and reprecipitation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate, filtration rejects sand, and carbonate addition recovers a calcium-rich precipitate in the receiver.

cases.title: Convert copper oxide through a soluble salt to a hydroxide
cases.original_physical_forecast: Acid dissolves black copper oxide; subsequent base addition forms a copper hydroxide-rich solid while preserving copper inventory.

cases.title: Zinc reduces two silver ions per atom oxidised
cases.original_physical_forecast: Zinc oxidation supplies two electrons per zinc atom, so the stoichiometric ceiling is two silver atoms deposited per zinc atom consumed.

cases.title: An active metal releases hydrogen from acid; copper is the control
cases.original_physical_forecast: Magnesium can reduce protons to hydrogen. Copper does not evolve hydrogen through the same proton-displacement reaction under ordinary non-oxidising conditions.

cases.title: Iodometric stoichiometry uses two thiosulfates per iodine
cases.original_physical_forecast: Thiosulfate reduces iodine to iodide; half the required dose should leave an oxidised-iodine pool, while the full nominal dose removes most of it.

cases.title: Ascorbic acid reduces iodine with a one-to-one molecular budget
cases.original_physical_forecast: Ascorbic acid is oxidised to dehydroascorbic acid as the oxidised iodine pool is reduced.

cases.title: Vitamin C has finite reducing capacity: iodine eventually persists
cases.original_physical_forecast: Successive iodine additions consume a finite ascorbic-acid pool. Iodine persists after that pool is exhausted.

cases.title: Acidified permanganate oxidises oxalic acid to carbon dioxide
cases.original_physical_forecast: Under a chemically appropriate acidic, warm setup, permanganate is reduced while oxalic-acid carbon becomes CO2.

cases.title: Changing the zinc half-cell shifts Daniell voltage in the opposite direction
cases.original_physical_forecast: Increasing zinc-ion activity with the copper side otherwise fixed lowers the forward Zn/Cu cell voltage according to the reaction quotient.

cases.title: A copper–silver cell links two different electron stoichiometries
cases.original_physical_forecast: The silver electrode is the more positive reduction half-cell; copper oxidation coupled to silver reduction has a positive forward driving force.

cases.title: Electrolysis connects charge to the hydrogen–oxygen gas ratio
cases.original_physical_forecast: For water electrolysis with a spectator sulfate electrolyte, net generated hydrogen and oxygen should have a 2:1 molar ratio and obey Faraday’s law.

cases.title: Dalton additivity after subtracting the sealed-air baseline
cases.original_physical_forecast: At approximately constant headspace and temperature, the pressure increments from added gases are approximately additive, with small gas-solubility differences.

cases.title: Dissolution makes carbon dioxide and nitrogen pressurise differently
cases.original_physical_forecast: More added CO2 is accommodated by dissolved inorganic-carbon species than an equal N2 dose, changing the pressure increment.

cases.title: Chemical absorption lowers carbon-dioxide headspace pressure
cases.original_physical_forecast: The alkaline liquid converts CO2 into bicarbonate/carbonate, storing more carbon in liquid and reducing the CO2 contribution to pressure.

cases.title: An acid trap captures ammonia as ammonium
cases.original_physical_forecast: Protonation stores ammonia as ammonium and reduces the uncharged ammonia fraction available to the headspace.

cases.title: Capture carbon dioxide and release the same carbon again
cases.original_physical_forecast: Base captures the CO2 dose as inorganic-carbon ions; acidification reverses that storage and moves carbon back toward molecular and gas-phase CO2.

cases.title: Degassing hard water promotes calcium-carbonate scale
cases.original_physical_forecast: Removing CO2 from a bicarbonate-rich calcium solution favours renewed calcium-carbonate precipitation.

cases.title: Catalyst particle size changes surface-controlled peroxide decomposition
cases.original_physical_forecast: At equal catalyst amount, smaller modelled particles expose more surface and consume more peroxide during the same virtual interval.

cases.title: Moderate warming accelerates the same manganese-dioxide reaction
cases.original_physical_forecast: The warmer heterogeneous-catalyst mixture reacts faster over a common short interval.

cases.title: The enzyme temperature response has an activity envelope
cases.original_physical_forecast: The source model predicts acceleration from room temperature to moderate warmth, but suppression in very hot water due to its enzyme-activity envelope.

cases.title: Recover and reuse manganese dioxide with a fresh substrate charge
cases.original_physical_forecast: The retained solid catalyst remains active when supplied with fresh solvent and peroxide.

cases.title: Acid activity, not acid bottle amount, controls a sulfur clock
cases.original_physical_forecast: Equal formal amounts of strong and weak acid give different proton activities and therefore different early thiosulfate-decomposition rates.

cases.title: Warming accelerates acid decomposition of thiosulfate
cases.original_physical_forecast: With similar acidity and substrate loading, the warmer mixture produces sulfur more rapidly over an early common interval.

cases.title: A second substrate pulse restarts an enzyme without adding new enzyme
cases.original_physical_forecast: The finite first substrate dose is consumed, but the enzyme remains available to process a second dose.

cases.title: Equimolar esterification reaches equilibrium instead of complete conversion
cases.original_physical_forecast: The declared ideal-mixture K ≈ 4 model predicts partial esterification, approximately two-thirds conversion for initially product-free equimolar reactants.

cases.title: Alcohol excess shifts esterification at fixed acid loading
cases.original_physical_forecast: The alcohol-rich mixture should convert a larger fraction of its fixed acetic-acid dose into ester under the ideal equilibrium model.

cases.title: Added product water suppresses esterification
cases.original_physical_forecast: Including water on the product side lowers equilibrium ester formation relative to the initially dry control.

cases.title: Base-limited ester hydrolysis leaves residual ester
cases.original_physical_forecast: The nominal hydroxide dose can hydrolyse at most half the ester through the saponification reaction, producing acetate and ethanol.

cases.title: Ester-limited hydrolysis leaves excess base
cases.original_physical_forecast: A sufficiently large hydroxide budget can exhaust the ester while leaving an alkaline product solution.

cases.title: Explicit alcohol oxidation is a requested model, not spontaneous vinegar formation
cases.original_physical_forecast: The explicit request converts ethanol and available oxygen into an acetic-acid/water product pool; the otherwise matched vessel has no organism or oxidation command.

cases.title: Overall glucose respiration preserves the six-carbon budget
cases.original_physical_forecast: The requested overall transformation can convert one glucose into six CO2 and six water molecules when oxygen is sufficient.

cases.title: Successive distillate cuts become poorer in ethanol
cases.original_physical_forecast: The earlier vapour cut is normally richer in the more volatile ethanol than a later cut from the depleted pot.

cases.title: Redistillation enriches a volatile component but sacrifices recovery
cases.original_physical_forecast: Redistilling the first condensate increases ethanol fraction in the second condensate, while only part of the original ethanol reaches the final receiver.

cases.title: A filter cannot separate two miscible liquids
cases.original_physical_forecast: Ideal filtration transfers the homogeneous ethanol–water liquid without selectively retaining one molecular liquid as a solid.

cases.title: Separate iron, sand and salt with three different physical operations
cases.original_physical_forecast: Magnetic collection isolates iron, filtration leaves a sand-rich residue, and evaporation recovers salt from the dissolved fraction.

cases.title: Determine chloride gravimetrically from a calcium-chloride sample
cases.original_physical_forecast: Two chlorides per calcium-chloride formula unit can yield nearly 0.002 mol AgCl, while a small silver excess remains in the filtrate.

cases.title: Both sugar and salt pass a filter, but only one is a strong electrolyte
cases.original_physical_forecast: Both dissolved solutes transfer with water; salt gives much greater conductivity because dissolution is not the same as ionisation.

cases.title: A separating funnel drains the lower liquid layer, not every liquid
cases.original_physical_forecast: A resolved water/hexane two-phase mixture can be separated by draining its denser aqueous layer while the organic-rich layer remains.

cases.title: Distillation simultaneously enriches ethanol and rejects salt
cases.original_physical_forecast: The distillate is ethanol-enriched relative to the starting liquid and strongly depleted in nonvolatile salt.

cases.title: Equal masses of water and ethanol have different heat capacities
cases.original_physical_forecast: Below phase transitions, the same energy pulse raises the temperature of ethanol more than that of the same mass of water.

cases.title: Hot copper and cold water equilibrate by heat capacity, not mass alone
cases.original_physical_forecast: The mixture should settle only a few degrees above the water’s initial temperature because water contributes much more heat capacity than the copper.

cases.title: Partial thawing spends heat without raising temperature
cases.original_physical_forecast: After creating an ice/water mixture, a smaller heating pulse melts part of the ice while the temperature stays near the melting point.

cases.title: Ice formation concentrates the remaining brine
cases.original_physical_forecast: Freezing removes mostly water from the liquid phase, increasing the concentration of salt in the remaining brine without creating salt.

cases.title: Cooling a hot potassium-nitrate solution recovers crystals
cases.original_physical_forecast: The decrease in potassium-nitrate solubility on cooling can produce crystals from a hot, initially more highly dissolved feed.

cases.title: Slaking lime couples chemical hydration to heat release
cases.original_physical_forecast: Calcium oxide reacts with water toward calcium hydroxide and an alkaline liquid; the real hydration reaction is exothermic.

cases.title: Heating bicarbonate generates carbonate, water and carbon dioxide
cases.original_physical_forecast: Crossing the curated thermal threshold converts bicarbonate toward carbonate with water and CO2 production; escaping products reduce the vessel’s retained mass.

cases.title: Ethanol’s boiling plateau is different from water’s
cases.original_physical_forecast: The energy pulse first reaches ethanol’s boiling region, then mainly drives vaporisation rather than heating all liquid far above its boiling point.

cases.title: Salt dissolution can warm one solution and cool another
cases.original_physical_forecast: Under the documented dissolution-enthalpy model, calcium chloride warms the water while potassium chloride cools it.

cases.title: Neutralisation calorimetry must subtract prior dissolution heat
cases.original_physical_forecast: Mixing separately prepared acid and base solutions releases neutralisation heat in addition to the sensible heat already stored in those solutions.

cases.title: A common ammonium ion suppresses ammonia ionisation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Adding ammonium chloride lowers the pH of an otherwise equal ammonia dose by shifting its base equilibrium.

cases.title: A basic buffer absorbs an alkali challenge
cases.original_physical_forecast: The buffered vessel shows a much smaller pH change than water receiving the same hydroxide dose.

cases.title: Reverse a buffer ratio while holding its total pool constant
cases.original_physical_forecast: Reversing an approximately 1:9 base/acid ratio to 9:1 raises pH by roughly 1.9 units in the ideal approximation.

cases.title: Diluting a buffer preserves its ratio but weakens capacity per volume
cases.original_physical_forecast: After splitting equal buffer inventories, dilution alone changes pH little. An equal acid challenge per approximate final litre consumes more of the buffer in the larger, dilute vessel.

cases.title: An extremely dilute strong acid never becomes a base
cases.original_physical_forecast: Water autoionisation prevents the naive pH = -log10(c_acid) calculation from predicting pH 8 for a 10^-8 M acid addition.

cases.title: Weak-acid dilution increases the fraction ionised
cases.original_physical_forecast: On tenfold dilution the pH rises less than a full unit in the ordinary weak-acid regime while the ionised fraction of the acid increases.

cases.title: Combine a weak-acid cation and weak-base anion
cases.original_physical_forecast: Comparable ammonium acidity and acetate basicity tend to give a near-neutral mixture while both weak equilibria remain active.

cases.title: Metal-ion hydrolysis acidifies ferric chloride
cases.original_physical_forecast: Ferric-ion hydrolysis acidifies the water much more than calcium chloride does; hydroxide-bearing ferric species or solids may also appear.

cases.title: A carbonate–bicarbonate buffer absorbs an acid pulse
cases.original_physical_forecast: A small proton dose mainly converts carbonate to bicarbonate, leaving an alkaline buffer rather than releasing all carbon as gas.

cases.title: Neutral water need not have pH seven when warm
cases.original_physical_forecast: For a temperature-dependent water equilibrium, warmer pure water has a lower neutral pH while hydrogen and hydroxide activities remain matched.

cases.title: Excess ammonia can dissolve a copper hydroxide precipitate
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chemical expectation: excess ammonia stabilises dissolved copper ammine species and can remove the hydroxide precipitate, with a changed copper colour.

cases.title: Selective hydroxide precipitation separates ferric and cupric ions
cases.original_physical_forecast: A moderately acidic endpoint should preferentially remove ferric hydroxide while leaving much more copper in the filtrate.

cases.title: Carbonate and sulfate precipitates respond differently to acid
cases.original_physical_forecast: Barium carbonate is acid-labile and can release CO2; barium sulfate should largely persist under the same dilute-acid challenge.

cases.title: Not every alkaline-earth sulfate precipitates at the same concentration
cases.original_physical_forecast: At these dilute analytical loadings, calcium sulfate is expected to remain mostly dissolved whereas barium sulfate precipitates strongly.

cases.title: Cross the silver-chloride ion-product threshold
cases.original_physical_forecast: The first trace additions are below the precipitation threshold; increasing both ion inventories crosses the solubility-product boundary.

cases.title: Selectively dissolve carbonate from a mixed mineral precipitate
cases.original_physical_forecast: Acid removes calcium carbonate from a mixture containing barium sulfate, after which filtration retains the sulfate-rich residue.

cases.title: One mixture can contain two distinct precipitates
cases.original_physical_forecast: Barium chloride supplies barium for sulfate precipitation and chloride for silver precipitation, yielding a mixed solid fraction.

cases.title: Iodide precipitation extends the silver-halide test
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chemical expectation: iodide and silver ions form poorly soluble silver iodide, commonly described as a yellow precipitate.

cases.title: Bromide precipitation without inventing an unregistered salt bottle
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chemical expectation: bromide from hydrobromic acid forms a pale silver-bromide precipitate with silver ions.

cases.title: Ferric ions oxidise copper without needing a noble-metal salt
cases.original_physical_forecast: Ferric ions can accept electrons from copper, producing ferrous and cupric ions rather than plating a second metal.

cases.title: Ferric ions oxidise iodide to iodine
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chemical expectation: ferric ions oxidise iodide while being reduced to ferrous ions, producing an iodine-containing pool.

cases.title: Neutral permanganate and ethanol produce a different manganese endpoint
cases.original_physical_forecast: The documented non-acidified teaching route forms MnO2 and an acetic-acid/acetate product pool, rather than treating every permanganate reduction as Mn(II).

cases.title: A zinc concentration cell reverses sign when electrodes are swapped
cases.original_physical_forecast: The concentration difference generates a non-zero voltage, and reversing the electrode order reverses its sign without changing the chemistry.

cases.title: Copper sulfate electrolysis competes with hydrogen evolution
cases.original_physical_forecast: With an inert-anode, copper-deposition interpretation, a small charge can reduce Cu(II) to copper while anodic water oxidation generates oxygen and acidity.

cases.title: Warm water retains a smaller fraction of a finite CO2 dose
cases.original_physical_forecast: Warming normally favours CO2 release into the gas phase. Pressure also changes directly with temperature, so phase inventories are needed to separate the effects.

cases.title: An inert gas at fixed volume changes total pressure, not the carbon dose
cases.original_physical_forecast: Adding inert gas to a fixed headspace increases total pressure without adding carbon. In an ideal mixture at fixed temperature, it does not directly multiply CO2 partial pressure.

cases.title: Stirring gives a bounded heterogeneous-catalyst rate enhancement
cases.original_physical_forecast: A vigorously stirred catalyst suspension is expected to consume peroxide faster than a minimally stirred one, without an unbounded proportional gain with rpm.

cases.title: Enzyme loading affects the early peroxide-decomposition rate
cases.original_physical_forecast: The higher catalase loading produces a larger early peroxide loss, before substrate exhaustion masks the dose response.

cases.title: Filtration distinguishes a soluble enzyme from a solid catalyst
cases.original_physical_forecast: An ideal filter retains solid MnO2 but passes molecularly represented catalase, so the two filtrates differ in catalytic activity.

cases.title: Equal time intervals consume progressively less substrate
cases.original_physical_forecast: With nearly constant catalytic conditions, a first-order-like substrate decay consumes less absolute peroxide in each successive equal interval.

cases.title: An iodine clock separates production from visible accumulation
cases.original_physical_forecast: Peroxide generates iodine while thiosulfate removes it. A larger scavenger inventory delays accumulation of an oxidised-iodine signal.

cases.title: A sulfur clock can become acid-limited before all substrate is consumed
